robots.name: Elixis-W
robots.note: Addverb page's W tab is JS-rendered; only the shared text 'Elixis-W: 10 kg payload, 1.5 m/s, ~2 h battery' was readable. Spec table read (1750 mm, 41 DoF, 75 kg) belongs to biped Elixis, not W. Aggregators report W tab as 1800 mm/210 kg/33 DoF — not verified, left null. Launched Feb 2026 (LogiMAT India), limited PoC deployments.

robots.name: Zippy (robotic sorter family)
robots.note: Zippy is a family of robotic sorters (Zippy 6/10/30/40 + Zippy X; Addverb blog also mentions Zippy 25) with payloads 6-40 kg; record kept at family level, so payload/dimensions/weight left out (Zippy 6: 6 kg payload, 510x475x235 mm, 20 kg, IP20 per its datasheet; Zippy 30: 30 kg, 710x655x550 mm, 24 kg; Zippy 40: 40 kg, 120-135 kg). Ground-marker (QR grid) navigation, differential drive, tabletop or floor configuration. Max speed 2 m/s and runtime up to 4 h are common to the variants per maker page.

robots.name: ALICE M1
robots.note: Wheeled (mobile) humanoid for manufacturing; height adjustable 130-180 cm. English page: 97 kg, 31 DoF (Korean page shows a different 160 cm/45 kg/41 DoF table, likely stale). Pre-order opened Oct 2025; URDF downloadable.

robots.name: H10-W
robots.note: Wheeled dual-arm assistant robot (differential base + lifting torso + two 7-DoF Diana 3 arms). Single-arm payload 3 kg rated / 7 kg max. Fast DDS and gRPC interfaces.

robots.name: Cobot Magic
robots.note: Mobile ALOHA-based bimanual teleoperation/data-collection platform: TRACER 2.0 differential base + 4x PiPER 6-DoF arms. Dims = stand frame 1125x758x1507 mm. Supports ROS 1/ROS 2, SDKs, LeRobot etc.

robots.name: AlphaBot 2
robots.note: Wheeled dual-arm humanoid (differential chassis, folding lift legs). Launch release said 34+ DoF incl. end effectors; hardware docs say 22 DoF excl. end effectors — used docs. spec: runtime 4–6 h (max used); battery_wh computed from 48V×30Ah; payload 4 kg rated per arm; wheel_count = 2 drive wheels (differential)

robots.name: AKINCI-5
robots.note: Official AKINCI-5 page: 42 kg, dimensions 52.5 x 27.5 x 129 cm (mapped to L x W x H), max speed 2.5 m/s (as stated - unusually high for a 129 cm biped, treat with caution), operating time 1.5 h, 30 min charge, Li-ion, depth camera, AKINCI UI / VR teleoperation. Project start 10.02.2025, completion 'ongoing'; page meta says 'coming very soon' -> pre-production. Bipedal ('mobile legs'). DoF not on official page (19 DoF comes from a company interview in press; aggregator 28 DoF/150 cm/50 kg and 175 cm/85 kg figures conflict and are not maker-stated).

robots.name: Romeo
robots.note: Aldebaran/SoftBank Robotics NAOqi 2.5 documentation (Romeo - Construction): height 1467 mm, mass 36.66 kg; Romeo is programmed through the NAOqi SDK (documented in maker's developer guide). Older press figures (~1.40 m, 40 kg) differ from the maker's documentation. Research prototype (project started 2009); no maker-stated release year, price or DoF captured.

robots.name: Hercules (H Drive)
robots.note: Amazon in-house drive unit (H Drive), not sold commercially; deployed only in Amazon fulfillment centers (status 'Commercial' here = in production use). First rolled out 2017 in Europe. Maker states 7.75 in tall (197 mm) and lifts 1,250 lb (567 kg). Aggregator figure 'weight 567 kg' is a mis-copy of payload - ignored. Navigates a fiducial-marker grid (per Amazon Science, not opened).

robots.name: Hypertron-T01
robots.note: Correction: skeleton category Quadruped, but maker describes it as a wheel-legged robot dog (轮足) - locomotion Wheel-legged. Maker spec table (Shenzhen Astrall/璇玑动力): standing 1110x610x745 mm, 82 kg incl. battery, working payload <=80 kg (200 kg static standing load), 4-8 h runtime (8 h = unloaded), 7 m/s max (lab conditions, limited in practice), 45 deg, 20-25 cm stairs, 90 cm obstacle, IP66, NMC 66.6 V 30 Ah battery (battery_wh = 66.6x30 = 1998 Wh, computed), secondary-development SDK supported. Conflicts: distributor-hosted manual/brochure state IP67, 16 DOF, 1130x620x730 mm, 64.8 V/23 Ah - maker web values used. 'Order now' button -> Commercial.

robots.name: Servi Q
robots.note: Unveiled at National Restaurant Association Show, May 2026 (co-developed with SoftBank Robotics, which launched it in Japan 28 Sep 2026). Weight conflict: Bear page 45 kg vs SoftBank Robotics JP spec 43.8 kg - used Bear value. Dealer listing claims 0.1-1.2 m/s; Bear states drive speed 0.7 m/s. Payload 10 kg per tray/shelf, 30 kg total; 1-3 tray configs. Min aisle 45 cm; can drive in reverse. 360° LiDAR per SoftBank (not opened) - not filled.

robots.name: Tiangong 3.0 (Embodied Tien Kung 3.0)
robots.note: Official name 具身天工3.0 / Embodied Tien Kung 3.0. Maker news (22 Apr 2026): 1.70 m, 64.5 kg, 43 DoF stated in news text (spec graphic per secondary sources says 31 DoF excl. hands - conflict; used maker news text 43, likely incl. hands). Max joint torque 400 N·m, Mid-360 LiDAR in head, optional six cameras, ran a half marathon. Spec image on product page could not be read as text.

robots.name: Tiangong Ultra
robots.note: Maker news (2025-04-19) states ~180 cm, ~55 kg, battery quick-swap, UWB-guided autonomous running; won 2025 half-marathon. Peak 12 km/h (3.33 m/s) is stated by Beijing E-Town gov't and Xinhua, not on the maker page opened — left out. CONFLICT: maker's own repost of Reuters (2026-09) covers the 2026 sprint build (100 m in 8.64 s); Reuters text elsewhere says that build weighs 75 kg and exceeds 17 m/s — the 2026 sprint version differs from the 2025 marathon build. No dedicated product page; not sold (delivered to research partners per aggregators, unverified).

robots.note: Maker site (bracketbot.com) has no product page or specs for 'Gen 2.5'; only a company statement. Model existence rests on the maker's X posts (1 Jul 2026: building 100 Gen2.5's; price 'less than $3000'), seen only in search excerpts, plus a later post naming 'Bracket Bot 1 Gen 3.0' — so Gen 2.5 may already be superseded. Self-balancing two-wheel (Segway-style) mobile manipulator per founder demos. Aggregator height 173 cm / $2k not maker-verified. Company HQ San Francisco (founder from Univ. of Waterloo; aggregators say Canada).

robots.name: Autopicker
robots.note: Wheeled mobile manipulator (AMR with in-aisle robotic picking arm) - current generation is Autopicker 2.0 (launched June 2025: +20% travel speed, 2x battery). Maker page: up to 12 h battery life, 1 h charge per 6 h work, SLAM + 3D vision navigation (no QR codes), 8 totes presented at G2P stations. FAQ: robotic picks up to 2.5 kg per item (not robot payload - payload left out). Price: RaaS from US$2,190 per robot per month (not a purchase price; price_usd left out). Company is Brightpick s.r.o. (Slovakia) / Brightpick Inc. (US; footer Austin TX) - country set United States with Slovak origin noted. Speed 1.2 m/s and 30 kg payload on aggregators are not maker-confirmed - not filled.

robots.name: Cartken Hauler
robots.note: Launched 9 Apr 2025. Maker figures conflict across its own materials: launch release says 7.2 km/h (2.0 m/s) top speed and 16+ h runtime (4 h recharge) - used here; newer Cartken homepage says runtime 12-14 h and the 2026 Hannover Messe one-pager says 6 km/h carrying / 5.4 km/h tugging, 98x55x102 cm, 190 kg (seen in search excerpts only, not filled). Payload 300 kg carrying (250 kg on 10° slope), 1,000 kg tugging. Omnidirectional wheeled, camera-based AI autonomy, indoor+outdoor. HQ Oakland CA (also Cartken GmbH, Munich).

robots.name: Yogi
robots.note: Model confirmed from the maker's own site via Wayback archive (cartwheelrobotics.com/yogi, Dec 2025 capture): companion humanoid with silicone skin, swappable battery, waitlist only. Company shut down Feb 2026 (founder's LinkedIn farewell, per Humanoids Daily); domain no longer the maker's. Status set Discontinued. Maker published no numeric specs; aggregator values (76 cm vs 150 cm, 8 kg vs 47 kg, 36 vs 50+ DoF) conflict wildly and were left out.

robots.name: CASBOT 02
robots.note: Maker's own DOF figures conflict: headline '≥37 DoF' vs 25 DoF (excluding hands) in its spec table; launch coverage said 33 DoF and 55 kg vs page's ~50 kg. Sold on JD.com.

robots.note: Wheeled-not-legged: differential-drive base, lift column and humanoid upper body. Height is a 112-2,100 mm range (max used).

robots.name: CASIVIBOT
robots.note: Out of scope-ish: an industrial inspection mobile manipulator, not a general humanoid. Not related to CASBOT despite similar names (some aggregators conflate them). Launched Aug 19, 2025; mass production from June 16, 2026. Maker says it moves autonomously; aggregators call it wheeled. No dimensions published.

robots.name: DriveMod Tugger
robots.note: Retrofit: Cyngn's DriveMod autonomy kit on a Motrec MT-160 tow tractor (vehicle built by Motrec, Canada). payload_kg = 500 lb deck load (226.8 kg); towing capacity is 12,000 lb (5,443 kg). Maker documents conflict on autonomous top speed: current product page and 2026 catalog say 4 mph (1.79 m/s, used); 2024 sheets said 2.7 mph and 4.5 mph, FAQ ~3 mph. Runtime: product page 'up to 12 h per charge' (used); 2024 sheet said 8 h. Dimensions 65 x 30 x 55 in; weight 1,250 ± 100 lb (567 kg) depending on options. Battery 48 V (Wh not stated). Sensors: 360° 3D LiDAR, 2D safety LiDAR (older sheet also lists RGB + ToF cameras). Price via EasyLaunch monthly subscription, no list price.

robots.name: Qiji XS
robots.note: DaxAI's own releases conflict on range: 100 km (WAIC, July 2026) vs 60 km (WRC, Aug 2026). Not yet shown running in public per press. Rideable mount, borderline scope.

robots.name: DR01
robots.note: Maker's own DR01 page (deeprobotics.cn/en/index/humanoid.html, Chinese mirror /robot/index/humanoid.html) and a maker news item (Aug 2024) confirm DR01 as DEEP Robotics' first bipedal humanoid, but both URLs now 404 / redirect: the redesigned maker humanoid listing (opened) shows only DR02, so DR01 appears superseded/no longer listed. Maker-stated: walking speed >1.6 m/s, 18 cm steps, 25° slopes, J60 + J100 joints (from search excerpts of the maker page; page could not be opened). Height 170 cm, 80 kg, 12 DoF, 15 kg payload, 2 h runtime are aggregator-only (humanoid.guide etc.) - NOT filled. Status set to Research (research/embodied-AI platform, never priced).

robots.name: Jueying Mini
robots.note: Values from DEEP Robotics' official Jueying Mini datasheet PDF (23 kg, 15 kg load in motion, 700x400x500 mm, 14,000 mAh, avg 2 h, 3.3 m/s, 35° slope). CONFLICT: the maker's legacy web page lists max load 10 kg, endurance 40 min and 30° slope. Battery voltage not stated so Wh not computed. Model no longer appears in DEEP's current product lineup (X50/X30/Lite3/M20/S10) - likely discontinued, status not stated by maker.

robots.name: Jueying X10
robots.note: DEEP Robotics' STAR Market prospectus (Sept 2026) states the Jueying X10 was launched in 2019 as its first industry-grade quadruped, with dynamic narrow-space traversal and autonomous charging, piloted for State Grid/China Southern Grid power inspection; succeeded by X20 (2021) and X30 (2023). No maker spec sheet found; figures circulating on aggregators (42 kg, 20 kg payload, IP66, 8 km/h) are unverified and left out. Not in current product lineup.

robots.name: DEXFORCE W1 Pro
robots.note: Wheeled-not-legged: dual-arm upper body on a differential or omnidirectional base. W1 Pro is the larger-workspace arm variant (W1 Core is fixed-station). No numeric size/weight on the maker page.

robots.name: Mech
robots.note: Wheeled dual-arm 'industrial superhumanoid': four-wheel-steerable rover base (moves, spins, strafes, climbs ramps) with two Kawasaki-built arms. Maker states 5.4 m armspan, 60 kg combined lift (Kawasaki release: 30 kg per arm), vertical reach >2.4 m, up to 16 cameras plus LiDAR, onboard 'supercomputer', operating 0-50 C, up to 1,500 m altitude (homepage says 5000 ft — minor conflict). Launched 17 Mar 2025; deployed for FedEx trailer loading and Sagawa Express validation.

robots.name: Diden Walker
robots.note: Not a humanoid: a magnetic-foot biped work platform (lower body + manipulator). Diden's separate 'Diden Humanoid' (175 cm, 90 kg) is a different robot. Exhibitor listing gives launch date Dec 1, 2026.

robots.name: Moxi
robots.note: Maker product page + Moxi 2.0 announcement (Oct 2025; rollout Aug 2026, NVIDIA Thor compute). Maker publishes no dimensions/weight/speed; aggregator figures (136 kg, 152 cm) left null. Category 'Indoor delivery' ok but it is a mobile manipulator (one arm).

robots.name: SkyWalker II (Tianxingzhe 2)
robots.note: DOF conflict within maker material: launch said 55 DOF (with hands); basic-version table says 29 DOF excluding hands (used). A half-body fixed-base version (103 kg) also exists. Price from CNY 158,000 (no USD). Launched Sept 24, 2025.

robots.name: SA01
robots.note: Maker product page (meta description) states SA01 is an open-source, highly extensible bipedal robot platform with 12 DoF, large quick-release battery and in-house straight-knee gait; maker purchase page lists CNY 42,000 (price_usd left blank — CNY list only). Maker development history dates release 29 Jul 2024. It is a legs-only biped platform (arms optional add-ons per maker launch coverage). Detailed spec tab is JS-rendered and not readable; aggregator values (129-138 cm, 40 kg, 1 m/s, 2-4 h) not filled. Maker press release (CES 2025, PRNewswire) says ~40 kg and <200 W walking power — weight not filled since only an approximate PR figure.

robots.name: ExR-2.5
robots.note: ExRobotics (Delft) product page: ATEX/IECEx Zone 1 + UL certified, -40 to +55 C, up to 2 km per charge, mission 2-6 h (runtime_h = upper bound 6), autonomous inductive docking, 4G/5G, 100+ robots deployed. Locomotion not stated in maker page text (US distributor MicroWatt calls it tracked) - left out; verify before setting Tracked. Speed 2 km/h appears in maker text seen only in a search excerpt (old /our-products page now 404), so max_speed_mps left out (would be 0.56). Weight 110-140 kg only on aggregators. Software via partner (page names Korial; older material Energy Robotics).

robots.name: FX Aegis Hyper
robots.note: Launched Sept 19, 2026. Maker says legged quadruped; Forbes calls it wheeled-legged (wrong). 85 kg is maximum payload; the shop page lists 20 kg (44 lb) rated, and 2.5 h runtime with payload.

robots.name: FX Navi
robots.note: Faraday Future store page: 12-DOF quadruped, ~8 kg, max 2 m/s, 34 cm obstacle, ~2 h runtime, battery ~0.2-0.3 kWh (range, battery_wh left out), Linux, open low-level interface + Python SDK, perception/compute via paired smartphone (AI compute 'not disclosed'), MSRP $1,990. Dimensions conflict: store lists L x W x H 112 mm (308 mm standing) x 298 x 515 mm, launch release says 46.5 x 20 x 51.5 cm - dimensions left out. Launched 16 Jun 2026.

robots.name: Figure 01
robots.note: Maker specs read from Figure's own 2023 homepage (via Wayback Machine, figure.ai no longer shows Figure 01): height 5'6" (1676 mm), 60 kg, 20 kg payload, 5 h runtime, 1.2 m/s, electric. Current figure.ai features Figure 03; Figure 01 superseded by Figure 02 (2024) -> status Discontinued (retired prototype/pilot, never sold). DoF figures in aggregators conflict (16 vs 40+ vs 41) and are not maker-stated - not filled.

robots.name: AICO 2
robots.note: Flexiv lists two AICO 2 variants: AICO 2-4 (2×4 kg payload, 281 kg, 6 h, dual-wheel differential) and AICO 2-10 (2×10 kg, 395 kg, 4 h). Variant-specific fields left null.

robots.name: Max 1500-L Slim
robots.note: Confirmed by ForwardX launch press releases (Nov 2023) and Max Series page. Naming: current maker page lists the model as 'Max 1500-L' (image labelled 'Max 1500-L Slim CE'); 'Slim' was the 2023 launch name. Width conflict: current maker page says 800 mm, older 2024 brochure/distributor (Roboware) says 850 mm - maker's current page value used. Max speed (1.1 m/s loaded / 1.5 m/s empty) and 48V 72Ah battery appear only on a Japanese distributor page - not filled. Sensors per maker page: 4 LiDAR, wide-angle cameras, optional 0-2 3D cameras, downward QR camera, odometer, IMU. One reseller (Logicbus) lists a non-CE variant as discontinued.

robots.name: GR-1
robots.note: Skeleton official_url (support.fftai.com/en/docs/.../GR-1_Introduction/) now 404s. Values from Fourier's own GR-1 brochure PDF (Feb 2024, fftai branding; hosted on edit.site CDN): standing size 1650 x 515 x 320 mm, ~55 kg (Pro ~60 kg), 5 km/h (=1.39 m/s), 3 kg single-hand payload, 44 actuators (GR-1, dexterous hands; GR-1L 34), 460 Wh battery, i7-13700H compute, RealSense depth camera, IMU, ring mic, 230 N·m peak torque. DoF conflict: brochure text says 'up to 54 DoF' (with 11-DoF hands) vs 44 elsewhere - used 44 (spec-table actuator count). Unveiled 2023; since succeeded by GR-2/GR-3. SDK (Python/C++) offered.

robots.name: FoxBot ATL (Mk3)
robots.note: Current model is FoxBot ATL Mk3 (autonomous trailer loader/unloader; Mk3 added loading, auto-adjusting fork tines, expanded sensors - maker blog Mar 2025). It is a retrofitted standard Class 1 three-wheel counterbalance electric forklift (manual driving still possible) - category is really autonomous forklift, not a typical AMR. Maker 1-pager: H 88 in (2235 mm), W 53 in (1346 mm), length with forks 110 in (2794 mm), 3,000 lb payload (1,361 kg), 16-18 h battery life (runtime_h=16; a Jan 2024 maker post said 18-20 h - conflict), operates down to -10 °C. Weight: Mark II user manual lists 7,189 lb excl. battery (excerpt only, older generation) - not filled. Top speed 2.35 m/s appears only on an aggregator - not filled.

robots.name: Futuring F2
robots.note: A wheeled dual-arm home robot per photos and press (maker text doesn't state the base type, so locomotion left blank); not a biped (some aggregators wrongly list 28-DOF biped specs). Released April 2026; maker price CNY 36,000 (no USD). Payload 3 kg at end effector; runtime >8 h.

robots.name: GoMate
robots.note: GAC Group official news pages (gacgroup.com/cn/news/detail?baseid=18961 and 19014) failed to load (HTTP 408 x3); search excerpts of those maker pages state: third-generation full-size wheel-legged humanoid, 38 DoF, variable wheel-foot structure (4-wheel mode ~1.4 m, 2-wheel standing up to 1.75 m), unveiled 26 Dec 2024, runtime up to 6 h. Values left out because page not actually opened. Locomotion is WHEEL-LEGGED (not bipedal). GAC also has a 4th-gen 'GoMate Mini' (1.7 m, 27 DoF, 8 h) per its HKEX filing - different model.

robots.name: Nexo
robots.note: Wheeled-not-legged: dual-arm humanoid upper body on a wheeled base. Unveiled at WRC, Aug 2026. Aggregator figures (168 cm, 85 kg, 200 TOPS, 5 km/h) conflict with Galaxea's page (1,700 mm, 2.5 m/s, 2000/700 TOPS); maker kept.

robots.name: Spirit 40
robots.note: Exists per Ghost Robotics' official YouTube channel; product page ghostrobotics.io/spirit-40 now removed (maker site lists only Vision 60) - likely discontinued, not stated. No official spec page reachable; aggregator specs (12 kg, 2 m/s) left null.

robots.name: Mini Hi (Xiaohai)
robots.note: Maker pages conflict: Chinese page 810 mm / 21.5 kg / 23 DOF / 1.15 m/s (used); older English page 890 mm / 20 kg / 27 DOF; WRC 2026 listing 82 cm / 17 kg. A 25-DOF Hi Pro exists. Runtime stated as '>1 h'.

robots.name: Q3-600D
robots.note: Latent (under-ride) lifting AMR. Model is listed on Hikrobot's LMR page and has a section in Hikrobot's LMR wiki; both pages render via JS so the fetch returned no spec text - values below come from the Hikrobot wiki parameter/intro pages as seen in search excerpts (maker-stated): 950x650x250 mm, 134 kg (distributors list 132 kg), 600 kg rated load, 60 mm electric lift, 2.0 m/s empty / 1.8 m/s loaded, differential drive, front laser + side ultrasonic + bumper. robots.note: Specs are the 2011 'all-new ASIMO' per Honda (130x45x34 cm, 48 kg, 57 DoF, 9 km/h, 40 min). Earlier versions differ (2000: 120 cm/43 kg). Honda ended ASIMO development (reported 2018) - status not set from an official statement.

robots.note: Maker site lists M-Bot only as 'Compact 2.5' humanoid' (~762 mm, converted from 2.5 ft), 'Coming soon', no specs or release date; it never appears in the maker's achievements timeline, so it likely never shipped. robots.name: Z-Bot

All products show 'Coming soon'. K-Scale Labs reportedly ceased operations Nov 2025 (third-party report) — status Discontinued. $999 price is press/aggregator-reported, not on maker page opened. robots.name: HUBO 2 (KHR-4)

robots.name: RHM-T1W
robots.note: Wheeled-not-legged. Maker spelling is Canop/CRP (Chengdu CRP Robot Technology). Maker's own figures conflict: launch article 1.9 m / 85 kg (used) vs earlier table 1,430-1,870 mm adjustable / 170 kg incl. 110 kg AMR base. Payload 5 kg per arm. Debuted Mar 2026, Hannover Messe Apr 2026.

robots.name: ARMAR-6
robots.note: CORRECTION: humanoid upper body on a holonomic (mecanum) wheeled base, not legged -> locomotion Wheeled. A later KIT paper states 28 DoF and a 40 kg battery pack (conflict on DoF; data sheet value used). Research platform of KIT H2T, not sold.

robots.name: ARMAR-7
robots.note: Wheeled-not-legged: humanoid upper body on a holonomic omni-wheel platform. 32 controllable DOF and 2.2 m/s from KIT's euROBIN entry; aggregators disagree on height/weight (170-175 cm, 70-120 kg), left out.

robots.name: RHP Bex
robots.note: Kawasaki's own blog (interview, 2023) confirms RHP Bex as a four-legged Kaleido derivative first shown at iREX 2022 (March 2022), with knee wheels for rolling on flat ground (wheel-legged). Payload is a development TARGET of 100 kg (stated as target, filled as payload_kg with this caveat); demonstrated carrying a rider. Upper body modular (offered as open platform for partners). Still under development - status Research; no dims, weight, speed or price published. Kawasaki's separate CORLEO rideable quadruped (2025) is a different product.

Conflict: maker press releases (PR Newswire Sep/Oct 2026, seen in search excerpts only) state 500 kg dual-arm payload; product page value (600 kg) used. Shown at WRC Aug 2026 and CIIF Oct 2026 with JD Industrial; no price/delivery date -> status left out (prototype-stage per press). Locomotion NOT stated by maker (press imagery suggests a wheeled base, aggregators call it humanoid) - left out; mobility should be checked before including in a mobile-robot catalog.

robots.name: Nori L2

Maker docs give 576 Wh battery (2x 24 V Li-ion in parallel), four 720p RGB cameras (two wrist, overhead, front), Raspberry Pi 5 onboard, Python/TypeScript nori-sdk; robot-side stack uses ROS 2 packages (ros2 run nori_cameras). robots.name: Wanda 2.0
robots.note: Wheeled dual-arm humanoid (differential drive). Height 1400-1680 mm via torso lift. Runtime 8-16 h (lower bound used). Payload = dual-arm. Presale Dec 2024; mass production Dec 2025.

robots.name: Autonomous Tugger (ATG)
robots.note: Vecna spec sheets. payload_kg = max tow payload 4,500 kg. Weight excludes battery. Speed conflicts across Vecna docs (6.0 mph/2.7 m/s on product page and one sheet; 4.5 mph/2 m/s on 2023 sheet); product-page 6.0 mph used.

robots.name: CPJ (Co-bot Pallet Jack)
robots.note: Maker sheets conflict among themselves: Mar-2026 tear sheet (used) 1740x927x2273 mm, 1.2 m/s, run time 4 h typical; 2024 sheets 1740x925x2195 mm, 1.25 m/s, 2.5 h; live product page '2.5 hrs quick-change battery'. Hot-swappable 24 V 60 Ah Li-ion (~1,440 Wh, derived). Collaborative: autonomous transport/drop-off, manual pick-up.

robots.name: Motion 1
robots.note: Model confirmed as a maker prototype: Vingroup (parent) 2025 annual report says VinMotion introduced the 'Motion 1 prototype' in 2025, developed in ~3 months (https://ircdn.vingroup.net/storage/Uploads/0_Bao%20cao%20thuong%20nien/2025/ENG%20Vingroup%20AR25.pdf, seen via search excerpt). Current vinmotion.net lists only Motion 2 and MiniMotion; the Motion 1 product page is gone (404) — Motion 1 appears superseded by Motion 2. No maker spec sheet for Motion 1 found; aggregator figures (175 cm, 70 kg, 2 m/s, ROS2) not maker-verified and left out.

robots.name: Motion 2
robots.note: Official vinmotion.net spec block for Motion 2: 1,632 x 489 x 253 mm (H x W x D), 63 +/- 1 kg, 29 DoF, arm payload 6 kg, speed 7.2 km/h (=2.0 m/s), runtime ~2 h walking / 3 h standing, knee torque 330 N·m, 1.5 h charge. CONFLICT: press/aggregators cite 178 cm / 75 kg / 31 motors / 40 kg lift - not maker-stated on current site. Bipedal. Vingroup annual report: prototype, mass production targeted end-2026.

robots.name: VNE40-66
robots.note: Maker page conflicts with itself on speed: headline 5.59 mph (2.5 m/s, used) vs 'up to 4.5 m/s forward' in its notes. Payload converted from the stated 6,180 lb.

robots.name: VNK 15
robots.note: Two maker pages differ: older page 1.8 m/s max driving speed; newer page 3.34 mph (1.5 m/s) under load.

robots.name: BabyAlpha (Dev-Q)
robots.note: Official page confirms BabyAlpha Dev-Q (developer edition) at ¥7,599; detailed spec table is JS-only, so dimensions/weight left null (aggregators list 516×298×308 mm, 7 kg, 120 min — not used).

robots.name: Titan o1
robots.note: Official name on wlrobo.com is '西湖o1' (Titan o1 per Westlake University press). Maker brochure: 29 self-developed integrated joints, knee peak torque 160 Nm, GAE avatar system, MagTap quick-swap interface, open sensor SDK. Height/weight not stated in text sources opened. humanoid.guide slug 'totan-o1' is a typo.

robots.name: THEMIS
robots.note: Values from THEMIS TH02 Gen2.5 brochure (2026). Earlier THEMIS V2 (2024 sheet): 22 DoF, 31–32 kg, up to 10 km/h (Professional). Gen2.5 differs; record reflects Gen2.5. speed: 5 km/h walking ÷3.6; battery 2×259.2 Wh hot-swap; endurance 120 min (180 with extended battery)

robots.name: ALLEX
robots.note: OUT OF SCOPE (not mobile): WIRobotics' own spec table states 'General-purpose humanoid robot upper body (Currently without lower body)'. Maker states hand/arm 15 DoF (English RIH page typo '115DOF'), >3 kg per hand, hook grip >30 kg, hand ~700 g, below-shoulder ~5 kg. Aggregator values (1650 mm, 55 kg, 43 DoF, 1.2 m/s, 120 min) are not maker-stated and were ignored. Unveiled Aug 2025 (press release). Category 'Humanoid' is fine but locomotion n/a.

robots.name: Sean (N1 / 小恩)
robots.note: Rename/correction: 'Sean' is the English name of Zeroth's N1 (小恩) home collaboration robot - NOT a 155 cm bipedal humanoid as aggregators claim. Maker-supplied IFA 2026 exhibitor copy: wheeled compact home robot, 30 kg, ~0.2 m2 footprint, 14 joints (telescopic left arm 4 joints, right cable-driven arm 7 joints, 3-finger gripper), 2-3 h active use, reach floor to countertop; detachable right arm. Launched at AWE 12 Mar 2026. No product page on zeroth0.com. Aggregator figures (155 cm, 45 kg, 16 DoF, 3 km/h) are not maker-stated.
